newsitem.title: USA: Duramed says will stay with plan for drug.
newsitem.headline: Duramed says will stay with plan for drug.

text.p: Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Monday it will stay with its business plan even though the Food and Drug Administration will not approve generic forms of the estrogen replacement drug Premarin.
Duramed has had an application for generic conjugated estrogens pending since September, 1994.
The company said it is evaluating its options for the product, and will make additional announcements in the future.

The company said alternative courses of action include instituting the studies encouraged by the FDA's center for drug evaluation and research, seeking a new drug approval for its conjugated estrogens product, appealing the FDA decision, or seeking approval of its product in markets outside the U.S.
"We are certain we have a sound, reliable, quality product," Duramed chairman and chief executive officer E. Thomas Arington said.
The FDA said Monday it would not at this time approve synthetic generic forms of Premarin because current data do not show that it has the same active ingredients as the brand-name drug.
Premarin is made by a division of American Home Products Corp.
